reasoning_thinking_help_lightbulb_toolti: What do Reasoning and Thinking mean?
reasoning_thinking_help_reasoning_desc: Injects an analysis prompt into the system prompt that instructs the model to respond in a structured, step-by-step manner. The model receives explicit instructions for methodical analysis.
reasoning_thinking_help_reasoning_effect: Effect: More structured, thorough responses through prompt engineering.
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_desc: Controls the model's internal chain-of-thought via the dropdown: "Off" disables thinking, "On" enables it at the model's default level. The model thinks in a hidden <think> block before responding. Only models with thinking support (e.g. Qwen3, DeepSeek) support this.
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_levels: Levels: Some models additionally offer graded thinking depth via their chat template — these appear automatically as extra dropdown entries (e.g. "max" on DeepSeek-V4 = Think Max with a considerably longer thought process and more tokens). Available levels are detected model-agnostically from the GGUF.
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_effect: Effect: Deeper analysis through internal reasoning. Produces longer responses and more tokens — higher levels accordingly more.
reasoning_thinking_help_both_on: Both ON: Maximum analysis depth – prompt instructions + internal thinking
reasoning_thinking_help_reasoning_only: Reasoning only: Structured responses without internal thought process
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_only: Thinking only: Internal CoT without additional analysis prompt
reasoning_thinking_help_both_off: Both OFF: Fast, direct responses without analysis overhead

casus_help_tooltip: What do these actions do? — Casus help
casus_help_intro: Casus collects motion and face events. You can run VLM analysis per event (sparkles button) or all at once — with cluster bundling so the VLM doesn't have to process each of 1000 similar frames.
casus_help_sparkles_body: Triggers VLM analysis for exactly this event. Loads the saved frame, sends it to the VLM (qwen3-vl), writes the description as a second line in the Person/Description column. Purple variant = already analyzed (clicking again overwrites).
casus_help_bulk_body: Bulk run: collects all events without description, groups them via pHash (perceptual image hash) + 5-min time-bucket per cam. VLM runs ONCE per cluster — description is copied to all members. Example: 1000 nearly identical desk frames → ~10 clusters → 10 VLM calls instead of 1000. VRAM is checked before start to avoid Ollama OOM.
casus_help_grouped_body: Switches display to cluster representatives. Instead of 1000 rows you see ~10 — each with a purple '+N' badge (that many more events belong to the same cluster). Useful after a bulk run to skim results without scrolling through repeats. Off shows all events individually.
casus_film_tooltip: Watch the film — browse all frames of this happening as a series
multipose_subtitle: Capture several head poses in sequence — this boosts recognition when the person later does not face the camera straight on.
multipose_no_preview: Pick an image source — live preview will appear here.
multipose_pose_left: Turn your head about 30° to the left.
multipose_pose_right: Turn your head about 30° to the right.
multipose_pose_done: All poses captured — save or add more.
vision_settings_face_recognition_help: Detects + identifies faces from the watch-mode stream. Low GPU cost, runs independently of the VLM.
vision_settings_face_continuous_help: Default: only on motion — GPU-friendly, ideal for entrance / doorman cameras. On: runs permanently — useful when still subjects should be recognized (desk cam).
vision_settings_feed_visible_help: Shows an accordion with the latest background events directly in the AIfred chat — useful when sources are set to 'Background' and you don't want the preview popup open all the time.
vigilantia_badge_window_tooltip: Events in the last 10 minutes (rolling window — counts down when it goes quiet)
vigilantia_feed_disarmed_hint: Vigilantia is disarmed. Click the eye in the mode row to start background detection.
vigilantia_feed_no_sources_hint: Master armed but no cam configured for background. Open Vigilantia settings and enable at least one source.
vigilantia_plugin_disabled_tooltip: Vision plugin is disabled — enable it under Plugins in the menu
vigilantia_help_intro: Three layers — master switch, per-cam config and live preview. This is where you see what is configured where, and when what happens.
vigilantia_help_section_master: 1. Master — the eye in the mode row
vigilantia_help_eye_open_body: Vigilantia is armed. For every cam enabled under 'Sources', a watcher runs. What triggers it depends on the camera profile: regular cams via the pixel motion detector, edge-AI cameras via their own on-device detection. Face recognition runs additionally if enabled in settings.
vigilantia_help_eye_closed_body: Vigilantia is off. No background watcher is running — neither motion nor face. Cams can still be started manually from the preview popup.
vigilantia_help_section_sources: 2. Sources — what the watchers do when running
vigilantia_help_sources_body: Per cam toggle: 'Background' on = this cam joins when the master is armed. Off = stays idle even if master is armed. Min motion sets how much of the image must change before a motion event fires.
vigilantia_help_motion_body: Pixel-based motion detector (OpenCV MOG2). Runs only for cameras without their own AI (profile webcam), on every frame of an armed watcher — edge-AI cameras trigger themselves (see below). Writes a 'Motion' event to Casus when image change exceeds the min threshold. Zones from the zone editor (ignore/ROI) apply exactly here.
vigilantia_help_person_body: YOLO11n body detector. Runs on motion IN PARALLEL with face recognition and detects whole persons — even with no visible face (turned away, far off). Writes a 'Person' event and, when the cam is armed, fires a proactive alert. Independent of identity — who it is is resolved by face recognition.
vigilantia_help_edgeai_body: Cameras with on-device detection (e.g. Reolink) report person/vehicle/animal themselves — AIfred polls their API state every 0.5 s and, on a hit, grabs wide + zoom frames in sync. Pixel motion detection and zones (except blackout) are off here; the local YOLO confirms the camera trigger, and face recognition runs on the zoom lens (more pixels on the face).
vigilantia_help_face_body: Vigilantia settings → 'Face recognition'. Off = faces are never detected (motion only). On = on motion events, InsightFace runs and a person event is written. 'Continuous' additionally = also without motion on every frame (for still desk cams).
vigilantia_help_preview_label: Vigilantia button in the input area
vigilantia_help_preview_body: Live cam feed where you can toggle Watch/Face on demand. Independent of master — for quick peeks without permanent arming. Pure live control, no permanent config.
vigilantia_help_personarium_body: Identity management — all recognized people, add or remove embeddings.
vigilantia_help_casus_body: Chronicle of all events — filter, delete, bulk-cleanup.
vigilantia_help_multipose_body: Guided enrollment capture with different head poses — for robust recognition when the person doesn't face the camera straight on.
vigilantia_help_lifecycle_link: ➜ When does InsightFace / VLM load? — see Model Lifecycle
model_lifecycle_help_title: Model Lifecycle — when does what load
model_lifecycle_help_intro: AIfred orchestrates four separate model families, each with its own load/unload strategy. This overview shows what occupies VRAM, when, and what triggers it.
model_lifecycle_help_base_size: Size: ~280 MB | Provider: CPU or CUDA (config: FACE_DETECT_USE_GPU) | Singleton per process
model_lifecycle_help_base_body: Lazy: loads on the first detect() call. Stays in RAM until restart (no automatic unloading).
model_lifecycle_help_base_triggers: Triggers: (1) Vigi master armed AND face recognition in Vigi settings ON → watcher calls detect() on motion. (2) Multipose enrollment. (3) Opening Personarium (re-match). (4) Live preview popup with face toggle ON. — Once loaded, the model stays even if all triggers go off again.
model_lifecycle_help_vlm_size: Size: 5-30 GB per model | Backend: Ollama | Manually unloadable
model_lifecycle_help_vlm_body: Lazy: loads on prewarm_vlm() call or first inference request. Unloaded via Ollama keep_alive=0.
model_lifecycle_help_vlm_triggers: Triggers: (1) Power button in Casus / Live preview popup → toggle_vlm_model_loaded. (2) Selecting a different model in the Vision-LLM dropdown auto-loads it. (3) Vision-mode switch on backend change. (4) Stress prewarm during calibration.
model_lifecycle_help_tts_title: 3. TTS (XTTS, Moss, Fishspeech, Qwen3Local, Piper) — speech synthesis
model_lifecycle_help_tts_size: Size: 0.5-7 GB per engine | Backend: Docker containers (except Piper which runs CPU-local)
model_lifecycle_help_tts_body: Container-based with refcount: ensure_engine_ready() starts container + waits for model load. acquire_tts/release_tts count users; at refcount=0 the container stops after keepalive timeout.
model_lifecycle_help_tts_triggers: Triggers: (1) First TTS synthesis call (chat reply with ★ prefix or direct generate_tts()). (2) Voice switch in TTS dropdown swaps engine. (3) Stress burn-in during calibration. — Piper is the exception: no container, loads instantly, no refcount.
model_lifecycle_help_llm_size: Size: 1-130 GB per model | Backend: llama-swap orchestrates llama.cpp instances
model_lifecycle_help_llm_body: Auto-managed: llama-swap loads models on-demand on every inference request and evicts them after idle TTL (config in ~/.config/llama-swap/config.yaml).
model_lifecycle_help_llm_triggers: Triggers: (1) Every user query loads the active Alfred LLM. (2) Automatik LLM loads only if it differs from Alfred LLM. (3) Model switch in the dropdown triggers a swap on the next request. (4) Other backends (Ollama, vLLM, Cloud) each have their own lifecycle strategy — Cloud loads nothing locally.
model_lifecycle_help_vram_body: Multiple model families can live on the GPUs in parallel (InsightFace + VLM + TTS + LLM). Calibration plans the layout in advance — see 'Calibrate context' in the settings panel. Rule of thumb: if VRAM is unexpectedly occupied, check in this order: Vigi master, VLM toggle, TTS voice, active chat (LLM).
model_lifecycle_help_tooltip: Model lifecycle — when does what load
audio_help_lifecycle_link: ➜ When does which TTS model load? — see Model Lifecycle
vision_settings_sources_help: Toggle per camera — enabled sources run in the background once Vigilantia is armed.
vision_settings_sources_empty: No image sources detected — plug in a webcam and trigger a rescan in the preview popup.
zone_editor_hint: <kbd>Left mouse button</kbd> paints the selected type, <kbd>right</kbd> erases.   Red = ignore motion  ·  Black = blackout (GDPR)  ·  Green = watch only this area (ROI).
zone_editor_ai_cam_hint: ⚠️ This camera detects persons/vehicles/animals itself (edge AI) — when armed, no pixel motion detector runs here. 'Ignore' and ROI zones only apply where the motion detector runs (e.g. in the preview popup). 'Blackout' always applies.
zone_editor_live: Live — paint over the areas you want ignored.
zone_editor_offline: Camera image not available (source offline?). You can still paint on the black grid.
zone_editor_no_source: No source_id parameter in the URL.
zone_editor_help_intro: Paint areas the background surveillance should treat differently. Left mouse button paints the selected brush type, right erases. Use the sliders for brush size and grid resolution.
zone_editor_help_red: Motion here triggers no alarm (e.g. swaying trees). The image stays visible and is saved.
zone_editor_help_black: The pixels are blacked out — only black is saved and sent to the vision model (GDPR, e.g. public street or neighbour's property). Motion there is suppressed too.
zone_editor_help_green: As soon as green cells exist, motion is evaluated ONLY there — everything else is ignored (e.g. only the entrance path). Green takes precedence over red.
zone_editor_help_controls: Mask active is the master switch: off = the whole mask has no effect but stays saved (counter-check). Saving takes effect immediately in the running watcher.
zone_editor_help_blue: Live motion versus the learned background. Paint areas that flicker constantly (trees, reflections) with »ignore motion« — the measured percentage then drops. Set the trigger threshold so the normal noise stays just below it.
zone_editor_help_threshold: Share of the image area that must change at once before the detection chain (person/face/alert) starts at all. LOWER = more sensitive: small or distant motion triggers too, but noise (light changes, leaves) fires more often. HIGHER = more sluggish: only large/near motion triggers — a distant person may stay invisible. Calibrate with »measured«: read the value during the target motion (e.g. a person at the end of the path) and set the threshold BELOW it, but above the idle noise.
zone_editor_help_ego: When the CAMERA itself moves (PTZ pan, auto tracking), the whole image shifts — the system detects this global shift, raises NO alert and relearns the new view immediately (instead of showing everything blue for minutes). Its threshold (watch.motion_ego_shift_px in the plugin settings, default 3 px) is the minimum image shift between two frames: LOWER = even tiny shifts count as a pan — careful: a mast swaying in the wind then resets detection constantly (detector stuck in warmup = blind). HIGHER = only fast pans are detected; slow pans cause false alerts again. In doubt the alert always wins, never the pan assumption.
vision_settings_source_background_help: Watch in background — starts automatically at AIfred service boot.
alert_rules_help: Which detections go to which channels. Image text = VLM description. One alert per happening (cluster).

vision_settings_face_retention_help: How long face crops, motion frames and DB events are kept. Cleanup runs daily at 03:00 local. Default 14 days.
calibration_hybrid_tooltip: Allow hybrid mode (offload layers to CPU when the model doesn't fit on GPUs alone). Off by default — hybrid inference is significantly slower and calibration itself takes much longer. Enable only for models larger than the total GPU VRAM.

calibration_vllm_burnin_title: Side-channel pairs (VLM + TTS on one card):
calibration_vllm_hint: Measures topology, speculation depth and chunk/GMU variants. Takes 30–120 minutes depending on model size and occupies every card.
calibration_reset_vlm_cache_tooltip: Clear the VLM burn-in table. Next calibration re-measures each VLM's VRAM footprint.
calibration_reset_tts_cache_tooltip: Clear the TTS burn-in table. Next calibration re-measures each TTS engine's VRAM footprint.

stt_condition_on_previous_hint: Required for the initial-prompt style (punctuation) to hold across the whole recording. Turn off if very long files start looping.

agent_editor_reasoning_tooltip: Enable reasoning — the AI thinks extensively before each tool call. More reliable for complex edge cases, but costs 30-120 s per turn extra.
agent_editor_cloud_model_hint: This system agent drives GPU calibration. It is not used in the chat — the calibration workflow invokes it when you select 🤖 AI as calibration mode in the Backend section. Based on VRAM measurements, the model iteratively decides on the optimal context and tensor-split configuration. Provider and model come from the same Cloud APIs as the main backend; the model list is fetched live. IMPORTANT: the model must support OpenAI tool-calling (the loop drives estimate/probe/finalize via tools) — plain chat or multimodal models (TTS/image/ASR) won't work. Stronger-reasoning models are more consistent but pricier. The prompt below is only stored in English because tool-use works more reliably on English with Cloud LLMs.

📄 Transcript saved: {transcript_link} ({chars}k characters).

The transcript is split by speaker: [SPEAKER_00], [SPEAKER_01], … These labels are anonymous — diarization detects WHEN someone speaks, not WHO they are. Map them to the real names mentioned in the conversation (greeting, introduction, form of address) and refer to people by name instead of “SPEAKER_00”.

Say e.g. “summarize {filename}”

or “translate {filename}”.
